name: Rest Lake
summary: Vilas County, Wisconsin: a 1912 ranger-station tower rebuilt by CCC crews in 1933-34 and moved in the early 1970s; old footings remain on a hill near Angler's.
design: 100-foot observation tower built by CCC enrollees in the winter of 1933-34, replacing a 55-foot windmill tower of 1912
status_note: Dismantled and moved in the early 1970s; the old footings remain on the hill beside Angler's on Tower Road.

access.note: Clio describes a town bike trail that follows the hill with the old footings, and a short climb that cyclists, hikers and diners can make.

visit.drive_up: Tower Road, Manitowish Waters (along the former Highway 10 frontage)
visit.trail_note: Short climb up the hill beside Angler's, on the town bike trail

events.note: Original tower: a 55-foot windmill tower with a makeshift cab, at the state ranger station
The state ranger station (not the tower) ended. The CCC history gives 1912 to 1923; Clio says removed by the early 1920s
Winter 1933-34: CCC enrollees from Camp Mercer dismantled the old tower and built a 100-foot observation tower. Clio's photo caption dates the new tower to 1934
Rangers lived on the forestry property near the tower until the 1950s. 1950 stands in for that decade; no exact year is given
Dismantled and moved to Harrison Hills, Wisconsin. Clio says early 1970s; 1970 stands in for that decade
